terms.meaning: The sum of the values divided by how many there are. It is also called the average, and is like a fair share.
The middle value when the values are put in order.
A graph of points joined by lines. It is good for showing change over time.
A computer table of cells that can work out values with formulas, such as totals and averages.

items.name: Finding the mean
items.formula: Mean = sum of values ÷ number of values

items.name: Mean as a balance point
items.formula: Distances to the left = distances to the right

items.name: Adding a value
items.formula: Above the mean raises it. Below the mean lowers it.

items.name: Adding a value equal to the mean
Adding the same number to all
items.formula: The mean increases by that number
items.example: Add 10 to each of 4, 8, 9, 11: the mean becomes 18.

items.name: Multiplying all by the same number
items.formula: The mean is multiplied by that number
items.example: Double each of 4, 8, 9, 11: the mean becomes 16.

items.name: Mean with frequencies
items.example: 3 families of size 4 and 2 of size 5: (12 + 10) ÷ 5 = 4.4

items.name: Median of an odd number of values
items.formula: Put in order and take the middle value

items.name: Median of an even number of values
items.formula: Take the mean of the two middle values

items.name: A very large value
items.formula: It moves the mean, but not the median
items.example: Change 20 to 100 in 3, 5, 7, 9, 20: the mean goes from 8.8 to 24.8, and the median stays 7.

items.name: Reading a line graph
items.formula: A steeper line means faster change
items.example: If a line goes from 10 to 40 in one year and from 40 to 50 in the next, the first year changed more.

items.name: Spreadsheet formulas
items.example: They give the total and the mean of the cells from B3 to G3.

mistakes.text: Put the values in order before finding the median. For 9, 3, 7 the median is 7, not 3.
With an even number of values there is no single middle value. Use the mean of the two middle values.
The mean need not be one of the values. The mean of 1, 2 is 1.5.
With frequencies, divide by the total frequency, not by the number of rows in the table.
